bugs.text: makeSprite returns `{c,w,h}` but `h` is never declared; the first call at line 44 throws ReferenceError 'h is not defined' at load, so the whole script (input, state, loop) never initialises. The page stays a black canvas forever.
Leftover placeholder `SPR.playerCap=makeSprite(SPR.player?null:0)` passes null as the rows array; even with the `h` bug fixed this line would throw TypeError (for..of on null) and still prevent load.
If the game ran, player-shot hitboxes are padded 1 px wider and 3 px taller than the sprite box, and ramming contact is padded 3/5 px, which is wider than the visible sprites.
If the game ran, the dual fighter fires both shots inside a `shots.length<2` check, so with one shot already in the air it fires a second volley of two, briefly allowing three shots on screen.

If the game ran, updateChal never calls updateEBullets or fmtUpdate and never checks enemy-body contact, so a challenging stage cannot hurt the player at all (acceptable) but the ebullets left from the previous stage are only cleared by setupStage.

summary: On paper this is one of the more complete designs: a 224x288 integer-scaled canvas, data-defined two-frame sprites for all three enemy types plus a red captured fighter, Bezier entry groups in the arcade order, sway then breathe, boss-plus-escort dives with 400/800/1600 scoring, a widening tractor beam with capture, rescue, docking and hostile-captive paths, challenging stages with wave bonuses and PERFECT, denominated stage badges, seven synthesized sounds, READY respawn and a correct fixed-timestep loop, all in a tidy state/update/render layout. None of it ever runs: the sprite factory returns an undeclared `h` (line 42) and the first sprite build at line 44 throws, so the page is a black rectangle with no title, no input and no loop, as the play test and nine identical black screenshots confirm. A dead placeholder line (45) that would also crash shows the file was never opened in a browser before delivery. As delivered it is not a game.
